topicName: Archimedes' Principle and Law of Flotation
description: This topic explains upthrust, Archimedes' principle, the law of flotation, relative density, and their applications to floating and sinking objects.

mcq.questionText: What is the name given to the upward force exerted by a fluid on an object placed in it?
mcq.explanation: The upward force a fluid exerts on a submerged or floating object is called upthrust or buoyant force.

mcq.questionText: Archimedes' principle states that the upthrust on an object equals the weight of the:
mcq.explanation: Archimedes' principle: upthrust on a body equals the weight of the fluid it displaces.

mcq.questionText: An object floats in a liquid when its weight is:

options.text: less than the weight of the object

mcq.explanation: The law of flotation requires the weight of a floating body to equal the upthrust (weight of fluid displaced).

mcq.questionText: An object weighs 50 N in air and 30 N when fully immersed in water. What is the upthrust on the object?
mcq.explanation: Upthrust = weight in air - apparent weight in water = 50 N - 30 N = 20 N.

mcq.questionText: Relative density of a substance is defined as the ratio of the density of the substance to the density of:
mcq.explanation: Relative density compares a substance's density with that of water; it has no units.

mcq.questionText: Why does a ship made of steel float even though steel is denser than water?

options.text: Its hollow shape displaces a large weight of water
The ship is pushed by wind

mcq.explanation: The hollow hull displaces a large volume of water whose weight equals the ship's weight, so it floats.

mcq.questionText: A device used to measure the relative density of liquids is called a:
mcq.explanation: A hydrometer floats in a liquid and measures its relative density using the law of flotation.

options.text: filling its ballast tanks with water to increase weight
removing all water from its tanks

mcq.explanation: Letting water into the ballast tanks increases the submarine's weight beyond the upthrust, so it sinks.

mcq.questionText: A solid of volume 0.002 m³ is fully immersed in water of density 1000 kg/m³. Taking g = 10 N/kg, the upthrust on it is:
An object sinks in a fluid when its density is:

options.text: less than the density of the fluid
equal to the density of the fluid
greater than the density of the fluid

mcq.explanation: If an object is denser than the fluid, its weight exceeds the maximum upthrust and it sinks.

options.text: hot air inside is denser than the surrounding air
the upthrust from the surrounding air exceeds its weight
there is no gravity at high altitude

mcq.explanation: Hot air is less dense, so the balloon's weight becomes less than the upthrust of the surrounding air and it rises.

mcq.questionText: The relative density of a metal is 8. If the density of water is 1000 kg/m³, the density of the metal is:
mcq.explanation: Density of metal = relative density × density of water = 8 × 1000 = 8000 kg/m³.

mcq.questionText: When a floating object is in equilibrium, the volume of fluid displaced has a weight that is:
mcq.explanation: By the law of flotation, a floating body displaces its own weight of fluid.

mcq.questionText: An egg sinks in fresh water but floats when enough salt is added. This happens because adding salt:

options.text: decreases the density of the water
increases the density of the water so upthrust increases
reduces the weight of the egg

mcq.explanation: Salt water is denser, so it provides greater upthrust which can now support the egg's weight.

mcq.questionText: Which statement about a body that just floats fully submerged (neither rising nor sinking) is correct?

options.text: Its density is much greater than the fluid's density
Its density equals the fluid's density
There is no upthrust acting on it

mcq.explanation: A body fully submerged in equilibrium has a density equal to that of the surrounding fluid.

fib.questionText: The upward force exerted by a fluid on an immersed object is called _____.
fib.explanation: Upthrust, also called buoyant force, acts vertically upward on objects in a fluid.

fib.questionText: Archimedes' principle states that the upthrust equals the weight of the fluid _____.
fib.explanation: The volume of fluid pushed aside by the object determines the upthrust.

fib.questionText: The law of _____ states that a floating body displaces its own weight of the fluid in which it floats.
fib.explanation: This law explains why ships and other floating bodies stay afloat.

fib.questionText: An instrument that uses the law of flotation to measure the relative density of a liquid is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A hydrometer floats deeper in less dense liquids and higher in denser liquids.

fib.questionText: Relative density has no units because it is a _____ of two densities.
fib.explanation: Dividing two quantities with the same units gives a pure number with no units.

fib.questionText: If an object weighs 12 N in air and 9 N in water, the upthrust on it is _____ N.
An object will float if its density is _____ than the density of the fluid.
fib.explanation: A less dense object weighs less than the fluid it can displace, so it floats.

fib.questionText: The upthrust on a fully immersed object can be calculated using the formula upthrust = ρVg, where ρ is the _____ of the fluid.
fib.explanation: Here V is the volume of fluid displaced and g is the gravitational field strength.

fib.questionText: A submarine controls its depth by changing the amount of water in its _____ tanks.
fib.explanation: Adding water increases weight to dive; removing water reduces weight to rise.

fib.questionText: The relative density of water is exactly _____.
fib.explanation: Since relative density compares a substance to water, water's relative density is 1.

tf.questionText: Upthrust always acts in the upward direction on an object in a fluid.
tf.explanation: The buoyant force is always directed vertically upward, opposing the weight.

tf.questionText: According to Archimedes' principle, the upthrust equals the weight of the object in air.
tf.explanation: Upthrust equals the weight of the fluid displaced, not the weight of the object in air.

tf.questionText: A body floats when its weight is equal to the upthrust acting on it.
tf.explanation: This balance of forces is the condition for flotation.

tf.questionText: An object always feels heavier when weighed in water than in air.
tf.explanation: An object feels lighter in water because upthrust reduces its apparent weight.

tf.questionText: Relative density is measured in kilograms per cubic metre (kg/m³).
tf.explanation: Relative density is a pure number and has no units.

tf.questionText: A steel ship floats because its hollow shape displaces a large weight of water.
tf.explanation: The displaced water's weight equals the ship's weight, satisfying the law of flotation.

tf.questionText: Salt water provides greater upthrust than fresh water for the same volume displaced.
tf.explanation: Salt water is denser, so the displaced water weighs more, giving greater upthrust.

tf.questionText: A hot-air balloon rises because the hot air inside it is denser than the surrounding air.
tf.explanation: Hot air is less dense, so the balloon's weight becomes less than the upthrust and it rises.

tf.questionText: An object whose density equals the fluid's density will remain floating fully submerged in equilibrium.
tf.explanation: When densities are equal, weight equals upthrust at full submersion, so it neither rises nor sinks.

tf.questionText: Upthrust depends on the volume of fluid displaced and the density of the fluid.
tf.explanation: Upthrust = ρVg, so both fluid density and displaced volume affect it.

summary.correctAnswer: The upward force a fluid exerts on an immersed or floating object.
summary.explanation: Also known as buoyant force, it opposes the object's weight.

summary.correctAnswer: Upthrust on a body equals the weight of the fluid it displaces.
summary.explanation: It applies to both fully and partly immersed objects.

summary.correctAnswer: A floating body displaces its own weight of fluid.
summary.explanation: Weight of the body equals the upthrust when it floats.

summary.questionText: Formula for upthrust on a submerged object
summary.correctAnswer: Upthrust = ρVg (fluid density × displaced volume × g).
summary.explanation: This gives the weight of the displaced fluid directly.

summary.correctAnswer: Upthrust = weight in air - apparent weight in fluid.
summary.explanation: The loss in weight equals the upthrust on the object.

summary.correctAnswer: The ratio of a substance's density to the density of water.
summary.explanation: It is a pure number with no units; water's value is 1.

summary.correctAnswer: Floats if less dense than fluid; sinks if denser.
summary.explanation: Density comparison decides whether weight or upthrust dominates.

summary.correctAnswer: It floats in a liquid to measure its relative density.
summary.explanation: It sinks deeper in less dense liquids and floats higher in denser ones.

summary.questionText: How a submarine dives and rises
summary.correctAnswer: It changes weight by filling or emptying ballast tanks.
summary.explanation: More water sinks it; less water lets it rise.

summary.correctAnswer: Its hollow shape displaces a weight of water equal to its own.
summary.explanation: The large displaced volume gives enough upthrust despite steel being dense.

hoq.questionText: A metal block weighs 60 N in air and 45 N when fully immersed in water of density 1000 kg/m³. Taking g = 10 N/kg, what is the volume of the block?
A wooden block of volume 0.01 m³ floats in water (density 1000 kg/m³) with 60% of its volume submerged. Taking g = 10 N/kg, what is the weight of the block?
hoq.explanation: Submerged volume = 0.6 × 0.01 = 0.006 m³; weight = upthrust = ρVg = 1000 × 0.006 × 10 = 60 N.

hoq.questionText: A solid of mass 0.8 kg and volume 0.0004 m³ is placed in a liquid of density 1500 kg/m³. Taking g = 10 N/kg, will it float or sink and why?

options.text: Sink, because its weight 8 N exceeds the maximum upthrust 6 N
Float, because its weight is less than the upthrust
Float, because the liquid is denser than the solid
Sink, because liquids cannot exert upthrust

hoq.explanation: Weight = 0.8 × 10 = 8 N; max upthrust = 1500 × 0.0004 × 10 = 6 N. Since 8 N > 6 N, it sinks.
